solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Add to enclosure

definitions.meaning: to add to something is to make it worse
a fenced or walled area holding buildings or animals

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: compound means aggravate or increase, and also a fenced-in area such as a prison yard.

clue.text: Girl, cold, left by Yorkshire river

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the Aire is a river running through Leeds in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A girl feels chilly after being abandoned on a Yorkshire riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Claire is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Equal pressure on amateur in type of golf game

parts.note: to match is to equal
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
lay means non-professional, as in a layman

explanation.surface: Levelling the stress on a non-professional golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Match play is golf scored by holes won rather than total strokes.

clue.text: Round and plump, and pompous

definitions.meaning: full and rounded, used of a rich deep voice
self-important and grandiose in manner of speech

explanation.definitionFit: Orotund describes a full resonant voice and also bombastic, inflated speech.

clue.text: Trap shortly set up — end of mouse!

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: soon means shortly, before long

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A mousetrap is set and will soon mean the end of a mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope used as a snare for animals.

clue.text: Small edition — short run

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a print or printing of a book is an edition of it

explanation.surface: A publisher describes a limited, small print run of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a short race run at full speed.

clue.text: Page awfully errant colleague

indicators.note: awfully suggests letters done badly, jumbled up

explanation.surface: A badly behaved page-boy is a wayward co-worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is an associate who works alongside you.

clue.text: Gutless deputy in bad poem

indicators.note: in puts the stripped deputy inside the word for bad

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill luck

indicators.note: gutless means with its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A cowardly assistant features in a terrible poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short pastoral poem depicting rural peace.

clue.text: Take charge after leader left nobbled

indicators.note: after places the charge behind the other piece
the leader having left means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: nobble is slang for steal, so nobbled means stole
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Someone takes command once the corrupted chief has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take charge' reads as one phrase meaning assume command, but 'Take' alone is the definition; 'nobbled' is slang for stolen, not tampered with.
explanation.definitionFit: Take can mean put up with or stand, as in cannot take the noise.

clue.text: Wager heads turned in chapel

parts.note: a bet is a wager

indicators.note: turned letters are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on a coin landing heads up in a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a common name for nonconformist chapels, especially in Wales.

clue.text: Early star or moon excited eminent scientist?

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An early evening star or the moon thrills a distinguished stargazer.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of EARLY STAR OR MOON rearrange into the answer. The question mark admits the definition is a description, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astronomer Royal is a senior honorary post held by a leading British astronomer.

clue.text: Provide improved accommodation for her over by river in York

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word her is read backwards

parts.note: the Ouse is the river flowing through the city of York

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a better home for a woman in York, beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehouse people is to move them into new, usually better, homes.

clue.text: Boxer's second name's Rex

parts.note: a handle is a slang word for a name or title
R stands for Rex, king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A boxer's cornerman turns out to be called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after name is just 'has' linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A handler looks after a boxer in the corner between rounds, the role of a second.

clue.text: Jokes about stable guy heading for reunion in best clothes

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jokes enclose the other pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes told by a comedian
a stable lad is a young worker who looks after racehorses

indicators.note: the heading for a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A stable hand cracks jokes while dressed up for a reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's smartest party clothes.

clue.text: Main article on damaged trailer

parts.note: a is the indefinite article in grammar

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper article reports on a damaged trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces, the article placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial road is a main road, a major route.

clue.text: Marsupials needing little time to find a place to sleep

parts.note: roos is short for kangaroos, pouched marsupials
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Kangaroos need a moment to find somewhere to bed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds settle to sleep for the night.

clue.text: What specialists know related in paper

parts.note: an expert is said to know their onions
kin means related, as in kin to someone

explanation.surface: Experts' knowledge is set out in a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Onionskin is a thin, translucent writing paper.

clue.text: One female in group is expelled

indicators.note: in places the one and the female inside the group

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians for example
I is the Roman numeral for one
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman in the band is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Banished means sent away, exiled or expelled.

clue.text: Donkey crossing near crevasse

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the donkey's word goes around the other

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
by means near, as in standing by the door

explanation.surface: A donkey is crossing close to a deep crack in a glacier.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a deep chasm, like a crevasse in ice.

clue.text: Section ready to house good soldiers

indicators.note: to house means to contain, so ready goes around the others

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
men is a common word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A unit prepared to accommodate decent troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a part or section of a whole.

clue.text: Send male in carriage

indicators.note: in places the male's letter inside the word for carriage

parts.note: transit means the carrying of goods or people

explanation.surface: A man is dispatched in a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to send on, as with a message or signal.

clue.text: Sustained energy at mains somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Power from the mains keeps going somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the ability to keep up physical or mental effort over time.

clue.text: Go to a nurse about onset of tonsillitis

indicators.note: about here means set around, so the first pieces enclose the letter

parts.note: to tend is to nurse or care for

indicators.note: onset of means the opening letter of a word

explanation.surface: A nurse treats a patient whose tonsillitis is starting.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to go to an event, as in attend school.

clue.text: A whole number one regent upset

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A ruling regent is overturned, leaving just one number.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a number with no fraction, a whole number.

clue.text: Noble Athenian — in fact, I'm one

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be a nobleman of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens, a wealthy Athenian, is the title figure of a Shakespeare play.

clue.text: Piece of furniture that now needs sides exchanged

indicators.note: exchanged means those two outer letters swap places
sides are the outer letters of the phrase, the opening one and the closing one

explanation.surface: Someone says a piece of furniture now needs its sides swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: Write THAT NOW as one run and swap its first and last letters, T and W: 'sides exchanged' moves T to the end and W to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a stand with open shelves for displaying ornaments.

clue.text: Slice boundary after wide

indicators.note: after places the boundary behind the other piece

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wide, a ball out of the batter's reach
an edge is a boundary or border

explanation.surface: A batter's slice goes to the boundary after a wide delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide and a boundary are both scoring events.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a slice cut from something round, like cheese or cake.

clue.text: Standard of old implements

definitions.meaning: the flag or emblem of the former Soviet Union
two tools, one for striking and one for cutting crops

explanation.definitionFit: The crossed hammer and sickle was the Soviet flag's emblem, and the words also name two farm and workshop tools.

clue.text: Give Spanish nobleman a note

parts.note: Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman or noble
te is a note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: A Spanish grandee hands over a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something, typically to a charity.

clue.text: Continued glowing over US state

indicators.note: over means covering, so the glowing word sits around the state

parts.note: red-hot things glow, so red means glowing
Maine is a state in the north-east of the US

explanation.surface: A glow lingered over an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Remained means stayed or carried on, a synonym of continued.
